title: Annotatio VI §.VII open: Wittenberger — Indigni Oral as proof presence is not imaginary
pass_a_gloss: §. VII. Moreover the most distinguished Wittenberger does not rest in the bare assertion of Corporal Eating of Christ’s body as belonging to the unworthy, but also strives to win Necessity and Fundamentality, as to Christian faith, for that Assertion — by this: that he thinks nothing stronger for proving that Christ’s body’s presence is not relative or merely imaginary, made by faith and thought, than if it be taught that even the unworthy and those without faith perceive Christ’s body and blood (§. XII).
pass_b_english: §.VII: the Wittenberger will not stop at bare assertion that the unworthy corporally eat Christ’s body.

He also tries to make that claim necessary and faith-fundamental — thinking nothing stronger proves presence is not relative or imaginary than teaching that even the faithless perceive body and blood (§.XII).
source_text: §. VII. Ceterum Clariss. Wittebergensis non in nuda assertione Manducationis corporis Christi Corporalis, indignis competentis, acquiescit, sed Necessitatem ac Fundamentalitatem quoque, quoad fidem Christianam, Assertionis illi, per id, conciliare studet, quòd fortius nihil opinatur esse, ad evincendum, præsentiam corporis Christi non esse relativam aut merè imaginariam, quæ fide & cogitatione fiat, quam si doceatur, etiam indignos & fidei expertes, corpus & sanguinem Christi percipere §. XII.
